newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks to reduce impact of its Okinawa troops.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks to reduce impact of its Okinawa troops.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it will cooperate with Japan in reducing the impact of American forces on Okinawa following a weekend referendum in which Okinawans voted heavily in favour of removing the troops.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters that "the results were not unexpected" but U.S. troops would remain in Japan.
"The United States will continue to cooperate with the government of Japan through the special action committee on Okinawa that was established by our two governments," he said.

"This is a process that we hope will help to calm some of the concerns of people on Okinawa," he said. "We seek to reduce the impact of the American military presence in Okinawa consistent with our responsibilities under the mutual security treaty that we have in place with the Japanese."
In a referendum on Sunday, 90 percent of Okinawans voted to reduce the U.S. troop presence.
Okinawa is home to three-quarters of all U.S. military facilities in Japan, although it represents less than one percent of the country's total area.

The non-binding referendum did not mean the immediate closure of bases, nor did it settle a year-long confrontation between Okinawa and the central government that was set off by the rape of a schoolgirl by U.S. servicemen last September.
A Japanese government spokesman said on Monday that the government took the outcome of the referendum seriously and would continue to deal seriously with the problems faced by Okinawa.
